Coolvibes source integration

Source: /Users/ersanyakit/Downloads/liquid_glass_widgets-main
Upstream pubspec version: 1.15.0
Runtime dependency: Flutter SDK only. No pub/path/git dependency is added.
Public entry point: lib/vendor/liquid_glass_widgets/liquid_glass_widgets.dart
Application adapter: lib/components/glass_surface.dart
All Dart library sources and shader includes are retained. Existing application
controls keep their APIs and gesture ownership; GlassSurface uses GlassContainer
and GlassGlow. General controls use premium refraction where supported. Chat
header controls, attachment/mic buttons and the input share the same frosted
material; modal surfaces use a stronger white tint (a dark tint in dark mode).
There is no claim of native UIGlassEffect or pixel-verified Telegram parity.

Local changes:
- Shader asset keys resolve to shaders/liquid_glass/ in both tests and runtime.
- Fixed two invalid relative imports in src/engine/glass_glow.dart.
- The project now pins Flutter 3.41.9 via .flutter-version and tool/flutterw.
  Flutter 3.41 includes iOS PlatformView rounded backdrop clipping (#177551);
  3.38 rendered rectangular blur over the WebView regardless of Dart clips.
  The previously adapted sampler calls still use SDK default filtering.
- PlatformView clips resolve capsule sentinel radii to real bounds before
  reaching the compositor (a 48pt circle has a 24pt corner radius).
- AppDesign owns one outer shadow for controls and input surfaces, based on
  Telegram GlassBackgroundView.generateLegacyShadowImage. Dark mode omits it.
- Input surfaces use the optical renderer with nonzero thickness, edge light
  and Fresnel, retaining their white blur tint. The role owns quality for both
  the field and adjacent/header controls; sheets retain their blur material.
- AppPressable owns the composer's passive press feedback: it observes pointer
  events without registering a competing tap or text-selection recognizer.
  Lift/release springs and directional stretch follow the local Telegram
  GlassBackgroundComponent/TouchEffect.swift reference. Reduce Motion suppresses
  the transform; up/cancel restore it. MessageField retains text-field semantics.
- AppTabBar forwards platformViewBackdrop over active maps; it no longer paints
  an opaque backplate. The shared control material maps its frost radius to the
  live backdrop filter over platform views, keeping the tint and shadow shared
  with map controls. The tab indicator retains its own icon-capture lens.
- iOS reserved-region bridge is compiled into Runner and registered manually;
  future SDK APIs remain guarded by upstream availability checks.
- Shader warmup runs before runApp; startup reports failures and keeps fallback.
- Action-sheet cards use shaped GlassContainer surfaces: the layer-only wrapper
  did not draw any backdrop blur at minimal quality. Tint is applied once.
- Application sheets share navigation.sheet, retain blur at the full detent,
  and let the sheet surface own the page backdrop.
- MIT notices: assets/licenses/liquid_glass_widgets.txt and
  assets/licenses/liquid_glass_engine.txt, also registered with LicenseRegistry.
  Engine attribution retained at src/engine/ATTRIBUTION.md.

Use the application's shared components for screens. The local public entry
point exposes the full set for extending those components without a package.
Do not introduce a second app-level button, header or glass renderer.

Verification:
./tool/flutterw test test/glass_source_integration_test.dart test/interaction_test.dart
./tool/flutterw analyze --no-pub

Observed verification (2026-10-25):
- All five shader programs compiled and preloaded in the integration widget test.
- Full test suite, concurrency 2: 233 passed, 2 skipped, no failures.
- Analyzer: no errors; 35 infos and one unused-import warning remain.
- iOS source bridge: swiftc -typecheck passed for arm64 iOS simulator.
- iOS 26.1 simulator build and input_runtime_test passed: chat chrome shares
  the input frost and shadow, a cancelled press did not send, a tap sent once,
  the full-height forwarding sheet retained its blur, and the nearby map's
  controls passed round-clip checks over a mounted WebView. The API is a
  fixture; this does not prove production backend delivery or pixel parity.
- No screenshot or pixel comparison was performed.
- Android arm64 debug APK built successfully. Android device interaction was
  not exercised; the APK build is compilation evidence only.

Nearby tab-bar follow-up (2026-10-25):
- 3 discovery-map tests passed, including light/dark real-Shell navigation,
  full-screen map bounds, translucent track, capsule blur clip and returning
  from another tab. Hidden check-in maps do not change the grid's glass mode.
- 15 shared chat-chrome, glass integration and press interaction tests passed.
- iOS input_runtime_test passed with the real Shell and mounted map WebView:
  dragging the tab indicator away from Nearby and tapping back retains the
  correct backdrop mode. Fixture API; no pixel comparison or Android device
  interaction was performed for this follow-up.

Input optics and pressure follow-up (2026-10-25):
- 25 chat-chrome, shared glass, press and composer-context tests passed.
  Coverage includes lift/stretch/release/cancel, text selection, focus, reduced
  motion, white tint, shared header/input material, send and voice gestures.
- The chat optical-input test in input_runtime_test passed on iOS 26.1 with
  preloaded shaders, measured press/drag geometry, one send, cancelled-send
  protection and the forwarding modal's blur. Installed Flutter SDK: 3.47.8.
- Analyzer reported no errors or warnings. No screenshot or pixel comparison.
